findings.finding: No actionable visible readability, blank-render, overlap, unintended text-clipping or page-overflow defect was found in the six-image pass.

The mobile figure view shows only the left portion of the 640px Figure 195. The right boundary truncates continuing strokes because inner horizontal figure scrolling is intentional. No offscreen pixels or scroll interaction are certified.

Despite their filenames, both supplied viewport images show the lesson opening. Judgments cover those actual visible pixels, not an unseen polarization section. Fixed viewport bottom cutoffs are not treated as page-content clipping.

limitations: Bounded pixel PASS for these exact six saved screenshots only; not complete-course, deployed-production, headed-browser or full English accessibility approval.

The provided report describes isolated offline headless native course HTML. No browser, application, additional test, dependency installation, database access, paid generation, commit or chat send was performed by this reviewer.

The mobile whole-page image was automatically resized by view_image from 390x8566 to 273x6000 for presentation. Its judgment is limited to that supplied preview scale, not a native-resolution certification of every small glyph. No reviewer-created resize, crop or derived image was made.
Figure 195 actual media width is 640px on desktop and mobile according to the supplied report and width-binding result; this reviewer did not rerun DOM measurements or width checks.
Only visible mobile figure pixels are judged. Offscreen right-hand labels and geometry, and the usability of horizontal scrolling, remain untested.

The historically approved Huygens Chinese-source-name parenthetical is intentionally retained and is not a prose revision request. Approved refraction derivation, source text, Chinese edition and figure science were not replayed or independently revalidated.
Machine Chinese aria metadata is disclosed by the text-only report and is not a visible display issue. Accessibility-tree content and full English accessibility are not certified.
